message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written move‑in checklist.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds any portion. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control). | • Report problems in writing (email or text) and give the landlord a reasonable time to fix them. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • If the landlord fails to repair, you may:
 1. **Withhold rent** (after giving notice).
 2. **Repair and deduct** (pay for repairs and deduct from rent).
 3. **Terminate the lease** (if the issue is serious). | • Keep receipts and document the problem. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | • File a complaint if the landlord repeatedly enters without notice or causes disturbances. | | **Notice Requirements** | • **Rent increases**: 30‑day notice for increases less than 10% of the current rent; 90‑day notice for increases of 10% or more.
• **Lease termination**: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month leases; 60‑day notice for fixed‑term leases. | • Verify the notice is in writing and delivered properly (hand‑delivery, certified mail, or email if agreed). | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Privacy** | • Landlords must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering your unit, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries and request a copy of the entry log if you suspect abuse. | | **Eviction** | • Landlords must follow the **Texas Property Code**: provide written notice (30 days for nonpayment, 3 days for lease violations, 30 days for no‑cause termination of month‑to‑month). | • Respond promptly to notices; seek legal counsel if you believe the eviction is unlawful. | | **Lease Terms** | • The lease must be in writing and include:
 - Rent amount and due date
 - Security deposit amount
 - Length of tenancy
 - Rules for pets, smoking, etc. | • Review the lease before signing; negotiate any unclear terms. | | **Pet Rights** | • Landlords may require a pet deposit or additional rent, but cannot refuse pets outright unless the lease specifically prohibits them. | • Provide proof of pet vaccinations and a pet agreement if required. | | **Subletting** | • You may sublet only with the landlord’s written consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld. | • Keep a copy of the sublease agreement. | | **Legal Remedies** | • **Small claims court**: recover unpaid rent or damages up to $20,000.
• **Tenant’s rights organizations**: local nonprofits often offer mediation and legal aid. | • Keep all documentation (rent receipts, correspondence, repair records). | #### Quick Checklist Before Signing a Lease 1. **Read the entire lease** – look for hidden fees, pet clauses, and notice periods. 2. **Ask for a copy of the move‑in inspection** – compare it to the move‑out inspection later. 3. **Confirm the security deposit limit** – ensure it matches Texas law. 4. **Verify the landlord’s contact info** – have a phone number and email. 5. **Check for “no‑cause” termination clauses** – they may allow the landlord to end the lease early. #### When Things Go Wrong | Issue | First Step | Next Step | |-------|------------|-----------| | Landlord refuses to return deposit | Send a written demand letter (include move‑in/out checklists). | File a claim in small claims court. | | Unresolved repairs | Send a written notice to the landlord; give 10–14 days to fix. | File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or seek legal advice. | | Unlawful eviction notice | Verify the notice meets statutory requirements. | File a lawsuit for unlawful eviction or seek mediation. | --- **Resources** - **Texas Property Code** – Chapter 24 (Residential Landlord‑Tenant Law). - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – [website](https://www.tchra.texas.gov). - **HUD – Fair Housing** – [website](https://www.hud.gov). - **Local tenant advocacy groups** – e.g., *Texas Tenants Union*, *Houston Tenants Union*. Feel free to ask if you need more specific guidance on any of these points!
